connections.label: Group / author
connections.title: Two scales of identity
connections.text: Distinct clothing separates people within the small group, while the large pale author name supplies a different kind of identification below.

descriptions: White intervals, counters and the outer field.
Animals and urban fragments forming the upper word.
The image fragments forming the lower word.
Whole visible flying silhouettes and the small bird imprint.
The heavy black author-name line.
Red award wording and bonsela-edition corner.
The lower review quotation and its attribution.

connections.title: Image becomes a readable title
connections.label: ZOO / CITY
connections.text: Animal and urban fragments accumulate into two readable words; comparing the rows reveals how local pictures contribute to larger letter shapes.

connections.title: Birds leave the letter boundary
connections.label: Birds / letters
connections.text: Small flying silhouettes extend from the dense upper word into white space, loosening the boundary between lettering and pictured environment.

descriptions: The open red and ochre spaces around the images.
Four upper figures, with dark hair and pale headwear retained.
The visible left profile, following the nose, lips and chin.
The right face and its complete visible hair silhouette.
Only the two irregular white dividing seams.
Large warm title letters in the lower panel.
Author line and upper endorsement wording.

connections.label: Profile / face
connections.title: Two different directions of attention
connections.text: The left profile points into the central interval while the right face turns more towards the reader, making the exchange deliberately unequal in orientation.

connections.label: Seam / title
connections.title: White divisions meet a gold title
connections.text: The irregular white seam separates the close-up faces from the even gold letter block, changing the cover's visual rhythm at that boundary.

descriptions: The dark textured field around the forms.
The visible hand and fingers, retaining rough interior colour.
The visible pink and red petals.
The dark and yellow flower centre.
White and yellow words near the top.
The yellow author name along the base.
The pale right-side source surface.

connections.label: Hand / flower
connections.title: Rough fingers beside soft petals
connections.text: Long rough fingers approach broad bright petals; their contrasting edges and surfaces create the central visual encounter.

connections.label: Centre / name
connections.title: Yellow links image and name
connections.text: The flower's tiny yellow centre and the wide yellow author line repeat a warm accent at two very different scales.

descriptions: The surrounding paper and visible copy edges.
The solid black field behind the portrait.
The source-visible hair outline and pale interior.
The pale face and hand, with their thin defining contours.
Red and yellow fragments within the portrait.
Thin Persian title lettering and the red heart.
The compact subtitle and author name.

Source pixels are assigned once, without filling occluded artwork. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. connections.label: Heart / portrait
connections.title: Warm colour crosses words and face
connections.text: Red and yellow move from the small heart within the Persian title to fragments of the much larger portrait below.

connections.label: Portrait / field
connections.title: A pale portrait needs a dark neighbour
connections.text: The solid black field makes sparse pale face and hand shapes readable, even where much of their interior remains the paper colour.

descriptions: Ochre sheet, surface texture and the retained dark photographic surround.
The dark standing figure, crossed feet and narrow warm outer contour, with visible text-shaped gaps.
Connected Persian title and dots remain together with the finer writing across the body.
The visible Latin-script exhibition title, dates, address, web addresses and two small event emblems.
The pale visible face inside the patterned head, without inventing detail hidden by the overprinted texture.
siam-mashq.methodNote: Five groups follow the visible figure, connected writing and event notice. The original museum reproduction is unchanged. Fine print texture and warm contour fringes remain; small writing is not reconstructed or presented as a complete transcript. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Body and writing
connections.title: A figure made into a reading surface
connections.text: Compare a broad dark shoulder with the large writing crossing the torso. The words alter how a familiar standing silhouette is read.

connections.label: Two kinds of encounter
connections.title: Face and exhibition notice
connections.text: The small pale face invites close attention above the practical dates and title. Portrait and announcement share one body.

labels: Festival lettering, dates and small emblems
Blue profile field and coral eye
Yellow sweep, diagonal and orange eye
Orange profile field and yellow eye
descriptions: The remaining printed panels and pale surrounding sheet stay with the photograph, including its visible mounting strips and lighting variation.
The visible festival announcement, ordinal, sponsor, small mask-like emblems, venue, dates and year are kept together as the information layer.
The left dark blue field retains its actual profile-like edge and the complete coral-ringed eye, including its dark centre.
The central yellow curve and diagonal retain their printed contours together with the orange circular eye and its centre.
The right orange field keeps its yellow-ringed dark eye and the thin blue notch at its left edge; the lower oval is separated as its own visible shape.
The continuous heart retains all four colour areas and the visible signature, without reconstructing any earlier or hidden colour state.
The tall narrow oval retains both the dark upper part and ochre lower part where it crosses the printed horizontal division.
festival-teatro-1968.methodNote: Seven visible groups are traced from the Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico photograph using observed contours and local colour comparisons. The entire uncorrected photograph is retained, including its mounting and perspective. Colour changes inside the heart and oval are preserved; they do not prove a specific sequence of ink overprinting. A source-specific local-contrast mask retains the low-contrast sponsor and venue/date lettering. The especially faint orange SE in SEPTIEMBRE remains a partly joined silhouette: its inner gaps cannot be reliably separated from this photograph. Original pixels, weathering and small edge fringes are retained. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Three circles
connections.title: Repeated eyes, changed contrasts
connections.text: Compare the coral ring around the left dark centre, the orange centre in the middle, and the dark centre inside the right yellow ring. A repeated construction changes colour, height and surroundings.

connections.label: One crossing, two shapes
connections.title: A shared baseline changes the colour
connections.text: The heart and the narrow oval both cross the same printed horizontal division. Their outlines continue while their colours change; compare how each shape stays recognisable.

connections.label: Information and image
connections.title: Small emblems and larger profiles
connections.text: Two small mask-like emblems sit near the top wording. The larger circles and angular edges below offer a visual comparison of scale, without claiming that the small and large forms depict named characters.

descriptions: The orange ground and unprinted margin remain behind the moving forms.
The many white curves and central pale opening share one plane.
The compact black body has a heavier visual weight than its companion.
The outlined figure crosses the red disc beside the solid silhouette.
Names and introductory words form a dense block at the top.
The angular title and small release information finish the lower edge.
vertigo.methodNote: The spiral is isolated by its pale printed ink; the two central bodies are traced separately. The red disc stays with the outlined figure, including its fine line work. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Solid and outline
connections.title: Two weights inside the same vortex
connections.text: The falling man is a dense black shape, while the adjacent woman is drawn largely in outline. The spiral holds these unequal visual weights close together.

connections.label: Type and motion
connections.title: Rigid names, rotating centre
connections.text: The stacked names and broad title act as anchors above and below the many curved spiral paths.

descriptions: The painted sky, fields and dark lower ground provide the setting.
The heavy beam cuts diagonally across the landscape.
The raised arm, face and magenta clothing form one continuous figure.
The two stacked white words occupy the upper right.
The smaller production names, lower titles and credit lines are kept together.
mother-india.methodNote: The visible beam and the complete foreground figure are hand-traced. Smaller lettering is isolated by its lighter ink inside its printed locations; the worn painted texture is retained. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Weight and effort
connections.title: A diagonal supported by a body
connections.text: The beam descends toward the woman’s shoulder. Her raised arm and the angle of her head make that long diagonal feel physically supported.

connections.label: Figure and headline
connections.title: Two forms that dominate the landscape
connections.text: The broad magenta torso and stacked white title are much larger, more concentrated shapes than the distant fields.

descriptions: The dark photographic surround and distressed pale border frame the close-up.
The left face and raised hand make the gesture of contact visible.
The smiling face, neck and shoulders form the brighter right-hand mass.
Widely spaced gold letters sit below the photograph’s strongest highlights.
The small award line, cast names and release information remain a separate reading level.
the-piano.methodNote: The photographic profiles are traced along visible contours, keeping the touching hand with the left profile. Their soft edges and shared shadows cannot establish original photographic layers; the untraced surrounding darkness stays in the field. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Touch and light
connections.title: The brightest area is the meeting of faces
connections.text: The two profiles nearly fill the picture. Their warm highlights meet around the cheek, mouth and raised hand rather than around a separate object.

connections.label: Quiet title
connections.title: Small letters below a large intimacy
connections.text: The gold title is spacious and low in the composition. Its modest scale leaves the close-up as the dominant encounter.

descriptions: Red windows, signs and street surfaces build the deep setting.
The front-facing child is traced as a distinct foreground figure.
The large pig at right and smaller visible pig at left share this plane.
The horizontal bar and visible uprights cross the figures.
The large white and purple title and fine lower information occupy the bottom.
The yellow vertical line and smaller white names remain separate from the scene.
spirited-away.methodNote: The child’s visible hair contour, body, pigs and foreground rail are traced independently. Neutral title ink and purple edging are separated inside the lettering region; warm skin and pink clothing are excluded from the white-ink rule. The rail retains its straight visible bars; the building signs remain part of the architecture. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: At the threshold
connections.title: The railing makes a foreground boundary
connections.text: The front-facing child and pig sit immediately behind the long horizontal bar. The glowing street recedes beyond this shared threshold.

connections.label: Two reading directions
connections.title: Vertical words above a broad title
connections.text: The narrow yellow line rises through the architecture, while the large white title spreads across the lower bodies and railing.

descriptions: The dark textured field retains distant streaks and smoke.
The long red ribbons curve around the central figure.
The expressive face, hair, arms, clothing and visible legs are kept together.
Bright flames and the lower circular wheel forms make the strongest light.
The gold English title occupies the lower right.
The upper campaign lines and small lower release words are isolated as lettering.
ne-zha-2.methodNote: The figure is traced from this edition. Ribbon paths and fire are isolated only inside their observed regions; dim smoke and distant streaks remain in the atmosphere. Bright fire overlapping the lower figure stays with the fire plane. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Curves and energy
connections.title: Ribbons widen a compact pose
connections.text: The face and torso sit near the centre, but the long looping ribbons spread their movement much farther across the dark field.

connections.label: Light below
connections.title: Fire connects the pose to the gold title
connections.text: The brightest orange light collects below and to the right of the body. The lower gold title repeats that warmth at a smaller scale.

descriptions: The yellow printed field, small lamps and worn paper remain behind the figures.
Repeated red venue names and black event words occupy the upper part.
A band of small black heads establishes a distant crowd.
The pale skirt and red patterned bodice identify the dancer.
The oversized grey man is cut along his hat, profile, body and extended hand.
The red lower words cross both figures and the yellow field.
moulin-rouge.methodNote: The front man and dancer follow their visible contours, with the advertising overprint removed to its own plane. The audience is isolated from the dark silhouettes in its observed band; yellow lamps remain with the ground. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Three distances
connections.title: Crowd, dancer and an oversized spectator
connections.text: The small dark heads sit far back, the pale skirt opens in the middle, and the large grey profile occupies the foreground. Their sizes create depth without a realistic perspective grid.

connections.label: Red repetitions
connections.title: The venue name becomes a rhythm
connections.text: Repeated red words at the top and lower red overprinting echo the dancer’s red bodice, carrying the eye through the yellow field.

descriptions: The red graphic panel and serrated yellow upper and side edges remain a single printed setting.
The overlapping riders are kept as a photographic group.
The large curved horns and skull are traced across the riders.
The motorcycle, road and surrounding lower landscape form the photograph’s remaining setting.
The white uppercase title is isolated from the red panel.
touki-bouki.methodNote: This small, visibly grainy edition uses a tinted photographic montage. The overlapping riders are kept together; the horn-and-skull motif is traced separately. The remaining motorcycle, road and landscape are explicitly retained as one photographic setting rather than presented as a cut-out object. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A broad curve
connections.title: The horns link the two halves
connections.text: The pale horns sweep across the riders and beyond their shoulders. Their width links the red upper panel to the motorcycle photograph below.

connections.label: One tint, one headline
connections.title: Yellow binds, white names
connections.text: The yellow treatment connects the riders, horns and serrated edge. The white title remains the cleanest, least photographic element.

labels: Black frame and pale upper panel
descriptions: The broad black surround and pale title panel frame the central picture.
The water and surface ripples retain their blue texture.
The shark is traced around its rising snout, jaw and visible body.
The small horizontal swimmer sits at the waterline.
The large red title occupies the pale space above the swimmer.
The tagline and lower cast and release information form a second textual frame.
jaws.methodNote: The swimmer and shark are traced from this particular framed edition. The shark’s underwater edges are soft, so its perimeter follows the visible blue silhouette rather than implying a recovered original cut-out. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Scale of threat
connections.title: A tiny horizontal body above a rising mass
connections.text: The swimmer extends sideways at the surface. Far below, the shark points straight upward and grows much wider toward the lower edge.

connections.label: Red above blue
connections.title: The title announces the collision
connections.text: The dense red word sits immediately over the narrow waterline. Its compact shape contrasts with the deep blue space that separates swimmer and shark.

descriptions: The cyan sky and light clouds remain behind the oversized letter.
The glossy pink and white letter serves as both title initial and physical stage.
The raised arm, seated pose and extended legs form the upper figure.
The reclining lower figure follows the curve of the letter.
White campaign words and small release details retain their separate hierarchy.
barbie.methodNote: Both people are traced around their visible poses. The oversized B follows its outer contour and retains its glossy internal highlights. The sky is excluded by its cyan colour only inside that contour; fine edge reflections remain source pixels. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A letter as a stage
connections.title: Two poses occupy one oversized initial
connections.text: The upper figure sits in the B while the lower figure reclines along its curve. A typographic form becomes a shared physical setting.

connections.label: Pink against blue
connections.title: A simple colour contrast makes room for detail
connections.text: The expansive pink letter is set against a clear cyan sky. That large contrast lets the smaller pale costumes and white words remain legible.

descriptions: The pale square fields remain the neutral base of the grid.
Black rectangles and descending triangles suggest a geometric hairstyle.
The central pale shape lengthens into a diagonal at the bottom.
Two eyes and a small mouth locate the expression with very little ink.
A purple forehead band and cyan circle form distinct upper accents.
Blue and green triangles meet a red lower block.
Small programme text occupies the upper-left square, with tiny lower printing information.
nihon-buyo.methodNote: The observed square grid and polygon edges determine the divisions. Facial marks are separated within their own positions, rather than collecting all red or all black pixels into colour buckets. The circle and band are described as visible accents, not as a claimed costume reconstruction. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Small expression
connections.title: A face located by three small marks
connections.text: Two compact eye forms and one red mouth turn a long pale shape into a face. Their scale is tiny beside the surrounding black geometry.

connections.label: Grid and diagonal
connections.title: A square structure with a descending face
connections.text: The upper fields follow a strict grid. Lower triangles redirect that grid into diagonals, extending the pale face toward the bottom edge.

descriptions: The dark field includes the printed surface and the circular door fitting.
A tall red strip provides a second background at the right.
The pale halftone face emerges from that red strip.
The narrow lamp links the upper wording to the smaller figure.
A full-length standing woman appears at a much smaller scale.
Large Chinese title characters, English words and small vertical credits form a separate reading plane.
the-goddess.methodNote: The large pale face is separated from the red printed panel through its local halftone contrast. The lamp and small standing figure are traced independently. The source’s print wear and limited resolution remain visible; the dark door fitting stays with the field. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two scales
connections.title: A face and a full-length figure
connections.text: The large face occupies much of the red panel, while the standing woman is slender and small. The contrast in scale makes the same sheet feel both intimate and distant.

connections.label: Vertical rhythm
connections.title: Words, lamp and body
connections.text: The narrow lamp and standing figure repeat the upright direction of the Chinese lettering. The broad face interrupts those thin vertical forms.

descriptions: The deep black field leaves a clear column for the typography.
The face and piled hair occupy the upper-left side.
The patterned dress, shoulders and arms extend to the lower edge.
Large white title letters create a strong horizontal line at upper right.
The framed review and smaller text form a dense second column.
black-girl.methodNote: The monochrome photograph is divided at the visible head, neck and clothing contours. The head and dressed body are analytical reading groups, not recovered photographic production elements. White lettering is isolated within its printed title and review columns. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Pattern and type
connections.title: Two textures share a dark field
connections.text: The bold dress pattern fills the left side while the smaller repeated white text fills the right. Both gain contrast from the surrounding black.

connections.label: A face beside a title
connections.title: Two competing first readings
connections.text: The face and the large uppercase title sit near one another at the top. One offers a direct human presence; the other gives a compact verbal identity.

descriptions: The unprinted paper remains behind the sparse graphic.
Red and black flame shapes stream toward the upper right.
The vertical fingers and descending dark arm form one visible gesture.
The crossing hand and diagonal right arm make the grip readable.
The diagonal black title is bracketed by thin red rules.
Small event information in red and the lower black imprint form the final reading level.
culture-and-resistance.methodNote: The two visible hand-and-arm gestures are traced across their shared grip, with the crossing hand in front. White interiors remain with each traced form; red flame, diagonal rules and event type are separated by observed position. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Grip and movement
connections.title: Interlocked hands beneath a streaming flame
connections.text: The hands concentrate the image into a firm central grip. Above them, the long red flame carries that compact gesture outward toward the right.

connections.label: Shared diagonal
connections.title: Arms and lettering point through the page
connections.text: The sloping forearm and rising title follow related diagonals. Thin red rules extend that direction into the open paper.

descriptions: The gold printed surface and surrounding glow remain as the base.
The sharply angled title occupies the top of the narrow sheet.
Long triangular rays extend through the upper architecture.
The visible tower fronts, bridges and side walls rise behind the portrait.
The metallic head, neck and shoulders form the principal foreground image.
Small production lines and the bold director line fill the bottom.
metropolis.methodNote: The roofline and robot contours are traced from this narrow edition. Upper triangular rays are separated where they remain visible around the buildings. Title ink is isolated within its observed angled extensions; lower text is kept separate without reconstructing covered shoulders. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Vertical monument
connections.title: The face repeats the architecture
connections.text: The robot’s long neck and central symmetry echo the tall tower behind it. Both are held within a very narrow format.

connections.label: Angles above curves
connections.title: The title introduces a hard-edged world
connections.text: The title’s abrupt angles connect visually with the triangular rays and tower roofline, before the rounded face changes the geometry below.

labels: Lower festival marks and release credits
descriptions: Luminous upper water, deeper teal below and distant fish form a continuous setting.
The dark cat, bright eyes, outstretched limbs and curved tail remain one figure.
Several prominent fish beside and across the cat make a nearer depth group.
The large rounded white title sits across the lower water.
Upper quotations and the Cannes mark occupy the pale water.
Lower festival marks and small release words form a fine-text base.
flow.methodNote: The cat follows its visible contour, including each separated leg and the tail. A few prominent fish are traced as a nearer group; smaller and blurred fish remain with the water. White title and fine lettering are isolated in their printed regions. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Bright eyes, dark body
connections.title: A face held inside a large silhouette
connections.text: The small gold eyes make the dark cat readable against the pale water. The limbs and tail extend that compact face into a much larger suspended pose.

connections.label: Different kinds of curves
connections.title: Brush letters beneath swimming bodies
connections.text: The rounded white title echoes the soft curves of the cat and surrounding fish, while its bright, opaque marks sit firmly across the deep water.

descriptions: The warm streaked ground supports the dense type-led layout.
Six distinct rectangular portrait panels make an ensemble across the top.
The large cracked English title forms a bowed graphic block.
Two lower script titles repeat the name at a smaller scale.
Blue production words, the format line and lower names contrast with the warm ground.
The black upper and middle headlines frame the portrait row.
sholay.methodNote: The six original portrait frames remain intact as explicitly named photographic panels. The cracked, bowed English title is retained as a graphic treatment, including its counterspaces and overlapping director line; it is not presented as six reconstructed type glyphs. Smaller scripts and blue format lettering are separated locally. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Ensemble and monument
connections.title: Small faces above an enormous name
connections.text: Six equal portrait frames establish a group. The much larger English title below changes the scale and makes the film name itself the main image.

connections.label: Repeated identity
connections.title: One name in three scripts
connections.text: The English display dominates, while Hindi and Urdu forms repeat the name along the lower edge. The blue production lines add a cooler accent to the red and orange sheet.

labels: Pale margin and dark montage field
descriptions: The pale paper and dark photographic field support the montage.
The smaller upper faces and the left-edge supporting portrait form an ensemble group.
The large left face and turned shoulder create one principal portrait.
The large right face, hat and pale coat create the other.
The angled handgun and gripping hand cross the lower-left portion of the montage.
The vivid red script spreads across the lower portraits and paper.
Tall cast names and smaller black production and release words frame the picture.
casablanca.methodNote: This is a blended photographic montage. The two large portraits, smaller ensemble and handgun are traced as visible reading groups, retaining shared shadows at their boundaries. Red overprinting and black words are isolated by their ink within the relevant positions; no hidden faces or coat areas are reconstructed. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Large and small faces
connections.title: The montage establishes a hierarchy
connections.text: Two large faces dominate the lower picture, while smaller supporting faces cluster above and to the left. The scale difference makes the principal pair immediately distinct.

connections.label: Script and structure
connections.title: Red lettering cuts across the monochrome image
connections.text: The flowing red title crosses the pale coat and paper. Its loose curves contrast with the rigid names above and the hard diagonal of the handgun.

descriptions: The pale paper, mosaic border, patterned halo and remaining architectural ornament.
The curved name band that frames the head.
The long green palm and its narrow stem, traced around the visible leaves.
The flower-crowned figure, richly patterned robe, sleeve and trailing hem.
The blue Gismonda lettering at the top of the narrow sheet.
The angular theatre plaque and small printer information at the foot.
gismonda.methodNote: Traced contours separate the standing figure, palm and angular theatre plaque; the curved name band retains its printed surrounding ornament. Fine source grain and printed outlines remain attached to their visible forms. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: An upright rhythm
connections.title: Palm and figure share the height
connections.text: The palm stem and the long robe repeat the same upward movement, giving the unusually narrow sheet a column-like rhythm.

connections.label: Names become architecture
connections.title: An arch above, a plaque below
connections.text: The curved name band encloses the head while the theatre plaque grounds the trailing robe. Lettering acts as part of the setting.

descriptions: The honey-coloured sky and narrow green field behind the seated pair.
The visible outline of the figure in dark clothing, including bent legs and bare feet.
The visible outline of the figure in a pale patterned dress, including the feet.
The broad white title and the small director line above it.
The horizontal timber boards supporting the pair.
The light production lettering printed over the dark boards.
sepet.methodNote: The two seated silhouettes are traced separately; their overlapping knees and sleeves remain with the person visible at that point. The lower right skirt contour leaves the visible grass on the field, and the platform follows the actual timber horizon. Bright title strokes retain their distressed edges without the cream strip below them. The small source limits the precision of soft photographic fringes. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two seated shapes
connections.title: Closeness through matching height
connections.text: The two heads and bent knees sit at similar heights. Their compact silhouettes make a shared group without a dramatic gesture.

connections.label: Light above and below
connections.title: A pale title, a pale dress
connections.text: The broad white letters and the light dress provide two quiet bright areas within the continuous warm scene.

descriptions: The red-orange setting and residual photographic texture around the figures.
The dark-haired figure partly obscured behind the foreground woman.
The woman’s large face, hair and visible neck at the top of the montage.
The floral garment, collar and overlapping hands in the foreground.
The white English and Chinese title lettering and main cast line.
The small festival mark, production text and bottom logos.
in-the-mood-for-love.methodNote: Traced visible portrait and costume regions follow this photographic montage. Where the two exposures blend, the boundary is an analytical contour rather than a claim of separable original photographs. White typography is selected only in its printed areas. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Overlap creates closeness
connections.title: Two faces share a warm field
connections.text: The rear face enters the space beside the woman’s neck and hair. The close overlap is more important than a clear boundary between bodies.

connections.label: Pattern meets type
connections.title: Dense flowers, clear words
connections.text: The floral costume fills the lower image with texture; the large white title cuts a much simpler shape across it.

descriptions: The warm ochre background surrounding the portrait.
The branching leaves, flowers and stems that crown the head.
The right-facing profile, pale hair and visible patterned clothing.
The narrow cream title letters and small film credit laid over the portrait.
the-color-of-pomegranates.methodNote: The profile and irregular botanical headdress are traced from the installed image. Cream title strokes are isolated within their own text regions, retaining only the visible lettering over leaves and skin. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: One edge, many branches
connections.title: Profile against foliage
connections.text: The face offers a single clear right-facing contour while the headdress branches in many directions. The contrast gives the dense image a readable edge.

connections.label: Straight and organic
connections.title: Letters cross the crown
connections.text: Narrow vertical letters repeat over the irregular leaves and flowers. The overlap makes the title and portrait read together.

descriptions: The warm paper, light interiors and remaining fine construction lines.
The red circular counterweight at the upper left.
The large black arc and angular upper profile.
The heavy black hooked form descending into the bottom of the sheet.
The red bar cutting diagonally across the construction.
The curved, tilted and stacked exhibition words, date and small bars that support them.
bauhaus.methodNote: Regional ink selections isolate the red circular form, red bar and two dominant black constructions. Smaller type is separated from the heavy geometry; fine rules and pale interiors stay with the paper field. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Repeated curves
connections.title: Circle and hook
connections.text: The open red circle and the black hook give the construction two large curved weights at different heights.

connections.label: Words join the structure
connections.title: The title follows the head
connections.text: The arched Bauhaus word follows the upper curve, while the diagonal exhibition words point along the construction beneath it.

descriptions: The cold-coloured sky and hot desert scene surrounding the main forms.
The two enormous yellow-orange MAD MAX lines.
The two main figures and the objects immediately grouped at their feet.
The chain entering diagonally from the lower-left edge.
The small top lines, Fury Road subtitle and production information.
mad-max-fury-road.methodNote: The two foreground figures and their immediate equipment are traced as one visible group. Regional colour isolation separates the giant title and supporting text; the foreground chain follows its diagonal path rather than a rectangular crop. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Type as scenery
connections.title: Figures in front of letters
connections.text: The figures interrupt the enormous yellow words, giving the title the role of a large plane behind the action.

connections.label: A route into the frame
connections.title: Chain and standing group
connections.text: The chain begins close to the lower-left edge and narrows toward the figures, adding a diagonal depth cue to the frontal lettering.

descriptions: The warm orange field and photographic crowd texture between the principal images.
The row of standing people that stretches across the top.
The large white Portuguese title.
The enlarged chicken with outspread wings in the foreground.
The fine top line, cast names, production block and small bottom marks.
city-of-god.methodNote: The ensemble and chicken are traced as visible photographic groups. The chicken’s soft moving wing edges retain a small amount of surrounding photograph; text is isolated regionally rather than by slicing the poster into bands. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A change of scale
connections.title: People and chicken
connections.text: The small standing ensemble reads as a horizontal group, while the enlarged chicken fills the foreground with a single spread gesture.

connections.label: A pause in the heat
connections.title: White title between images
connections.text: The white title places a strong readable interval between the group above and the restless orange texture below.

descriptions: The cream paper border and yellow sky visible through the tree.
The pale city, dark dome, blue buildings and horizontal wall.
The warm orange slopes and paths in front of the city.
The trunk, canopy and dark foreground ground that frame the view.
The cream Visit lettering above the lower name panel.
The large dark blue Palestine letters in the cream base panel.
visit-palestine.methodNote: The dark framing tree is selected within its own foreground regions. Traced city and land contours retain the landmark and paths as visible groups. The two printed invitations are separately isolated from their panels. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A view through a frame
connections.title: Tree and distant city
connections.text: The dark trunk and canopy surround a much lighter city. The opening makes the buildings feel farther away than the foreground tree.

connections.label: Two kinds of blue
connections.title: Landmark and place name
connections.text: The dome and blue architecture create a compact dark accent in the city; the large blue place name repeats that weight at the bottom.

descriptions: The green hillside, sky and diagonal bridge around the main figures.
The large central warrior, raised arm and visible sword.
The enlarged face and surrounding hood on the right.
The smaller people and scenes gathered around the warrior’s legs.
The deep red Japanese title down the left side.
The light vertical credits, cast information and lower production text.
seven-samurai.methodNote: The central warrior and large right-hand face are traced separately from the smaller action collage. The lower scenes stay grouped where they overlap. Regional ink selection isolates the red title and lighter credits without inventing covered figures. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A diagonal and an upright
connections.title: Gesture meets title
connections.text: The raised arm and sword pull the eye diagonally while the deep red title holds a strong vertical position at the left.

connections.label: Several scales of drama
connections.title: Large faces, small scenes
connections.text: The large warrior and right-hand face tower over the smaller lower scenes, giving the sheet more than one scale of storytelling.

descriptions: The dragons, eyes, swirls, small objects and residual collage surrounding the large visible groups.
The upside-down portrait and the fan of repeated arms entering from above.
The round central title field and the words it contains.
The large upright woman in a red vest, her raised hands and visible lower arms.
The two large sideways and lower-left portraits.
The large sideways and lower-right portraits.
The hat-wearing, shadowed figure behind the upright portrait.
everything-everywhere-all-at-once.methodNote: Seven deliberately selected visible groups make this dense collage readable: the two opposing main figures, two side portrait groups, shadowed central figure, title medallion and surrounding ornament. Small interwoven cameos remain in the ornamental world. Group contours retain nearby printed detail at blended edges. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Opposing orientations
connections.title: An upright and an inverted portrait
connections.text: The main portrait rises from below while the inverted figure enters from above. Their opposing directions meet around the central medallion.

connections.label: A quiet centre
connections.title: Title within a busy world
connections.text: The compact dark title sits in a clear circular field, surrounded by repeated eyes, curves and crowded portraits.

descriptions: The blue-to-cream sky and warm outer paper border.
The enlarged locomotive, its wheels and the diagonal rods across the foreground.
The pale plume following the engine’s long diagonal.
The thin light lines and small insulator shapes converging on the right.
The large geometric Nord Express title.
The smaller border destinations, railway names and artist lettering.
nord-express.methodNote: The locomotive follows its outer silhouette; the steam is a narrow irregular contour along the diagonal. Light telegraph lines and title ink are selected in their own regions, while route lettering is isolated on the actual border. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Direction shared
connections.title: Steam and wires draw the distance
connections.text: The steam follows the engine’s diagonal, while the telegraph lines narrow toward the lower-right distance. Both make the static sheet feel directional.

connections.label: Engineered lettering
connections.title: Name above machine
connections.text: The broad geometric title and oversized wheels use simple, weighty shapes at very different scales.

descriptions: The large stone face, rough textures and smaller architectural scenes around the people.
The bare-chested foreground fighter, bandaged fist and visible clothing.
The fighter behind, with raised arms and a black sleeveless top.
The smaller group of people at the lower right.
The large white Thai title, red underline and small English name.
The top lines, short line above the title and lower production marks.
ong-bak.methodNote: The two main fighters have separate traced visible silhouettes; the smaller right-hand people remain a shared montage group. The stone face and other small scenes stay in the setting. Soft blended photographic boundaries are retained, with no reconstruction behind the figures. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Arms set the direction
connections.title: Two gestures cross the upright frame
connections.text: The foreground fist reaches toward the viewer while the rear fighter’s arms run across the image. The contrasting gestures provide the movement.

connections.label: Light on two surfaces
connections.title: Skin against carved stone
connections.text: The bright foreground skin separates from the larger, rough stone face behind it, even though both share the warm brown palette.

descriptions: The bed, blinds and simulated worn-paper edge around the principal forms.
The red cover-like masthead and its small dark editorial lines.
The giant yellow Pulp Fiction title.
The reclining portrait, bent legs, raised cigarette hand and hand on the book.
The foreground handgun and the visible printed paperback beneath the hand.
The price circle, cast list and small production information.
pulp-fiction.methodNote: The portrait is traced around the hair, legs and hands. Separate irregular contours isolate the gun and visible book, while yellow title and cast lettering are selected within their printed areas. The red masthead follows the cover’s actual colour break. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Cover hierarchy
connections.title: A masthead before a face
connections.text: The yellow title over red reads at a glance, before the darker photographic scene and outward-looking portrait below.

connections.label: Competing clues
connections.title: Portrait and foreground objects
connections.text: The handgun and paperback sit close to the resting hand. Their small, sharp shapes compete with the larger portrait for attention.

descriptions: The pale dunes, warm atmosphere and thin printed frame.
The dark standing figure, with visible hands cupped around the light shape.
The bright sphere held in the hands and its smaller counterpart on the sand.
The large widely spaced Yeelen title across the top.
The film credit and laurel at left, review at right and lower cinema information.
yeelen.methodNote: The child follows the visible head, ear, elbow, hands, hanging cloth, bent leg and cropped foot; the open gaps between limbs stay with the sand. The held sphere follows its visible finger-occluded boundary, retaining the illuminated palm with the child. Lower credit strokes are selected by local contrast within observed text lines, leaving broad dune shading on the landscape. Photographic softness remains at the original pixel resolution. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A repeated light
connections.title: Two spheres at different scales
connections.text: The bright shape in the hands repeats as a smaller pale circle on the sand. Their size difference carries the eye across the open ground.

connections.label: Wide and upright
connections.title: Title across a solitary figure
connections.text: The spaced title stretches across the horizontal sheet while the dark body provides a concentrated vertical shape beneath it.

descriptions: The pale station structure, receding rails and visible space around the montage.
The engine and receding passenger train on the left.
The enlarged standing portrait in the upper right.
The overlapping lower pair and the visible knife in the foreground.
The dark slanted title and name banners with their white lettering.
The dark lower strip containing the production credits.
cairo-station.methodNote: The train and three principal portrait regions are traced as visible montage shapes. Dark typographic bands follow their slanted printed outlines. The station framework and rails remain behind them; no obscured parts are reconstructed. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two kinds of diagonal
connections.title: Title bands and track lines
connections.text: The slanted dark title bands introduce a direction that returns in the receding rails below.

connections.label: Scale tells the story
connections.title: Faces dominate the engine
connections.text: The enlarged upper portrait and foreground pair occupy more visual space than a realistic station view would allow, bringing emotion forward.

descriptions: The pale paper and narrow edge surrounding the three principal elements.
The large solid red disc in the upper half.
The five linked gold rings, including their visibly overlapping strokes.
The tall gold Tokyo 1964 words at the bottom.
tokyo-1964-first-poster.methodNote: Regional pigment selections isolate the sun, linked-ring emblem and event lettering. The photographed paper texture is retained in every selected stroke and in the surrounding field. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Circles with different roles
connections.title: Solid disc and open rings
connections.text: The large filled disc and the smaller open rings repeat circular geometry while differing in weight, scale and colour.

connections.label: A three-part stack
connections.title: Symbol, emblem and event
connections.text: The broad disc narrows into the ring group, then the tall event lettering forms a firm base at the bottom.

descriptions: The dark textured background around the spare composition.
The large cool blue Priester brand name.
The upper red match and its yellow head.
The lower red match and its yellow head.
priester.methodNote: The blue wordmark and each complete match are isolated using local colour and contour selections. Each yellow head stays with its red shaft, preserving the product as two distinct objects rather than separate colour bands. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two nearly parallel lines
connections.title: A small diagonal creates movement
connections.text: The two matches point down toward the right at slightly different angles, giving the otherwise spare layout a gentle directional pull.

connections.label: Name and product
connections.title: Cool letters above warm objects
connections.text: The cool blue name forms a broad stable shape above the warmer red and yellow matches.

descriptions: The dark field binds the otherwise separate faces and text blocks.
A left-facing portrait occupies the first third of the photographic strip.
The central face turns toward the right, framed by deep shadow.
A tightly cropped face completes the strip at the right edge.
White “amores” and red “perros” share one compressed line.
The award line, review quotations and fine credits surround the image.
amores-perros.methodNote: The three portraits are read as the visible photographic passages in the horizontal montage. Near-black shadows remain with the black ground; this small 220-pixel-wide source does not support hair-by-hair extraction. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Three directions
connections.title: A conversation across the strip
connections.text: The three cropped faces point and look in different directions. Their shared warm light joins them even as the black intervals keep each face distinct.

connections.label: Red returns
connections.title: A word echoes the surrounding print
connections.text: The red half of the title repeats the red award and review text. White lettering gives the other half of the title a different emphasis against the same dark ground.

descriptions: Fine cracks and the pale vertical seam establish an overhead ground.
The long red motorcycle stretches across the upper part of the sheet.
A smaller red-clad figure walks toward the machine.
Red Japanese lettering overlaps the heavy black title.
The compact credit stack and fine bottom line complete the print.
akira.methodNote: The motorcycle and figure follow their visible silhouettes, including the printed cast shadows. The red and black title is separated from the pale pavement by its printed ink; the fine cracks stay with the ground. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two red scales
connections.title: The machine is larger than the walker
connections.text: The same red links the long motorcycle to the much smaller figure below it. Their difference in scale makes the overhead space immediately legible.

connections.label: Red meets black
connections.title: The image colour becomes lettering
connections.text: Red moves from the motorcycle and jacket into the Japanese title, where it crosses the dense black letterforms.

descriptions: A hazy street and lower fire frame the confrontation.
The open jaws enter from the upper right and project thin strands into the sky.
The woman and rifle make a diagonal silhouette across the lower half.
Large, softly edged white letters occupy the central gap.
Festival, cast, filmmaker and release lines form smaller centres of attention.
hope.methodNote: The creature and armed figure use traced visible contours. Saliva is retained where it can be distinguished from the sky. Hair, smoke and the lower figure dissolve into the photographic atmosphere, so the analysis keeps those soft transitions approximate. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Opposing diagonals
connections.title: Two edges close in on the title
connections.text: The jaws descend from the upper right while the rifle rises from the left. The pale title occupies the opening between those opposing diagonals.

connections.label: Light at the centre
connections.title: The quietest shape is a word
connections.text: The large white title is simpler and lighter than either textured figure. The smaller white notices repeat that contrast at the top and bottom.

descriptions: The generous pale field gives the red mark room to dominate.
Closely packed hand-drawn letters form an irregular, continuous red mass.
A small flag and its upright pole rise above the joined letters.
“POLSKA ’80” and tiny printer and signature marks sit away from the central word.
solidarnosc.methodNote: The red ink is divided at the visible junction of the flagpole and wordmark. The flag is an inseparable part of the printed logo, so this division is for close reading rather than a claim about how it was produced. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Joined strokes
connections.title: A flag grows out of the word
connections.text: The upright pole appears to rise directly from the crowded letters. The same red joins the flag and word into one emphatic sign.

connections.label: Large and small
connections.title: A second scale of reading
connections.text: The small dark date in the lower right is separated from the large red word by a wide pale interval. Its scale asks the viewer to move from recognition to closer reading.

descriptions: Sea, sky, clouds and warm sand form a continuous illustrated setting.
Outstretched arms, a red scarf and lifted boots describe the figure’s leap.
Oversized cream “G.N.R.” initials sit high against the sky.
Green destination lettering gives the scene its place and promise.
Irregular pools on the beach echo the blue-green sea.
skegness-is-so-bracing.methodNote: The fisherman and four visible pools are traced as illustrated silhouettes. The cream railway lettering and green slogan are isolated only within their printed text areas; beach texture and the small artist mark stay with the setting. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A leap in the landscape
connections.title: The pools make the lifted boots legible
connections.text: The fisherman’s boots rise above the irregular beach pools. Those grounded shapes help us read his curved body as a leap rather than a standing pose.

connections.label: Green echoes
connections.title: The destination shares the figure’s palette
connections.text: The green jumper and green destination line repeat a colour already present in the sea. The small red scarf interrupts this otherwise restrained palette.

descriptions: Buildings and a pale street give the central figures a receding setting.
A tall brown-coated figure dominates the foreground.
A smaller boy looks upward beside the coat.
A back-turned figure and bicycle occupy the lighter distance.
The red title spans the bottom of the illustration.
Black credits and the circular upper-right mark frame the image.
bicycle-thieves.methodNote: The father, boy and receding bicycle group follow the visible painted forms. Some soft paint and paper around the distant bicycle remain attached because the installed 220-pixel-wide reproduction cannot resolve every spoke or brush edge. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two heights
connections.title: An upward glance meets a long vertical
connections.text: The boy’s face sits low beside the long coat and turns upward. The difference in height directs attention from the smaller figure to the taller one.

connections.label: Foreground and distance
connections.title: A bicycle recedes behind the figures
connections.text: The smaller back-turned figure and bicycle are lighter and farther up the street. They add a second scale behind the close foreground pair.

descriptions: Vertical green and brown brush marks carry through the surrounding field and hair.
A closely cropped face occupies most of the sheet.
A pale form curves over the left forehead and across the lower foreground.
Outlined fingers appear along the lower left and right edges.
White title lettering and small yellow festival and release lines sit over the painting.
joyland.methodNote: The source is a small, visibly painterly reproduction. Boundaries follow the central face, pale overlapping forms and visible fingers without assigning an identity or action to the ambiguous painted embrace; brush texture crosses those analytical boundaries. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Curves across a face
connections.title: The pale form redirects the portrait
connections.text: A pale curve crosses the left forehead and returns across the lower foreground. It interrupts the otherwise direct, tightly cropped face.

connections.label: Letters over paint
connections.title: A quiet title over busy brushwork
connections.text: Thin white title letters sit over the pale lower form. Their regular spacing contrasts with the dense vertical strokes in the painted face.

descriptions: The flat yellow field makes the figure and navy headline easy to distinguish.
White words occupy a broad navy speech bubble with a downward-pointing tail.
A red scarf with pale spots frames the hair and face.
The face and curled hair form the portrait at the upper left.
Large blue folds describe the work shirt and rolled sleeve.
The raised fist, flexed arm and other hand define the central gesture.
A small emblem and production lettering occupy the lower blue band.
we-can-do-it.methodNote: The headscarf, face, shirt and arm gesture are traced separately because their overlap explains the pose. The illustrated sleeve edge, loose hair and paper texture remain approximate at pixel scale; the speech bubble is kept intact with its message. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Words and gesture
connections.title: A raised arm answers the headline
connections.text: The flexed arm lifts toward the speech bubble. The bubble’s tail points back down toward the portrait, linking message and gesture.

connections.label: Three strong colours
connections.title: The scarf is a small, bright interruption
connections.text: The red patterned scarf is much smaller than the blue shirt or yellow field. Its concentrated contrast draws attention to the face.

descriptions: The pale sheet and thin black frame contain a dense illustrated montage.
The large central figure holds two guns and strides across the lower lettering.
A stack of records and a smaller seated figure form a rounded mass at the right.
Smaller figures and a motorcycle scene surround the central body.
Heavy black outlined lettering steps down and across the sheet.
Black and red taglines, cast names and production lines surround the pictures.
harder-they-come.methodNote: The central figure is traced around its guns and flare. The smaller painted scenes are grouped as the visible action montage, while records and their seated figure form a separate group. Soft montage overlaps and the paper’s fold lines are retained as printed, without reconstructing hidden bodies. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Figure breaks the type
connections.title: A stride crosses a stepped title
connections.text: The central figure’s long legs cross the low title lettering. The line break in the title leaves room for this vertical movement.

connections.label: Music and action
connections.title: Round records beside a long figure
connections.text: The dark circular record stack balances the tall central figure. Its rounded edges contrast with the guns, legs and block lettering around it.

descriptions: A dark field surrounds the lanterns and the architectural corner.
The yellow upper panel carries two strong lines of Chinese text.
A chain of red lanterns decreases in size down the left side.
A seated figure and patterned chair occupy the lower right.
Large red Chinese characters create a vertical divider.
Smaller pale and red text blocks occupy the spaces around the pictures.
raise-the-red-lantern.methodNote: The nested lantern silhouettes, the seated figure with its chair, and the actual yellow header panel are separate visible groups. The very small installed image merges fine chair edges with the adjacent architecture; those soft boundaries are approximate. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A descending sequence
connections.title: Lanterns make depth through scale
connections.text: The lanterns become smaller as they descend. The red vertical title repeats their direction while holding a steady character size.

connections.label: Two kinds of weight
connections.title: A bright chain balances a dark figure
connections.text: The red lantern chain occupies the left side while the subdued seated figure anchors the lower right. The dark interval between them leaves the vertical title clearly visible.

descriptions: The black surround and cream border frame the central painted window.
A diagonal stair rail leads toward a small backlit silhouette.
A large red-haired portrait dominates the lower centre.
A hat-wearing figure and gun enter from the left.
Smaller figures gather in and below the dark right-hand opening.
An oversized red 3 extends below the other title letters.
Pale cast names and small production lines surround the illustration.
the-third-man.methodNote: The illustrated window is separated from its printed surround, then divided into the portrait, left figure, right montage and stairway scene. The stairway retains its small backlit silhouette. Painted shadows cross figure boundaries, so these are visible montage groups rather than restored individual character drawings. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Three scales
connections.title: A large face, small figures and a distant shadow
connections.text: The large portrait sits close to us, the right-hand figures are smaller, and the stairway silhouette is smaller still. Scale changes turn one flat window into several depths.

connections.label: A falling numeral
connections.title: The title enters the picture
connections.text: The red 3 drops below the rest of the title into the pale top of the picture. The diagonal stair rail then carries the eye toward the distant silhouette.

descriptions: A muted grey surround remains visible around the central tilted field.
The large pale diamond establishes the main diagonal geometry.
Small single and paired coloured diamonds scatter across the white field.
The concert details are set on the same diagonal axis near the lower left.
musica-viva.methodNote: The large tilted field and the individual printed geometric motifs are separated from the grey surround. Motifs are kept as complete small signs, including paired colours, rather than sorted into generic colour planes. The diagonal text stays together as one reading block. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Repeated angles
connections.title: Small signs repeat the large field
connections.text: The small diamonds repeat the angles of the much larger white diamond. Their varied spacing makes a loose rhythm inside a strict geometry.

connections.label: A shared diagonal
connections.title: Type follows the picture’s axis
connections.text: The concert lettering tilts in the same family of diagonals as the diamond edges. The text therefore belongs to the composition rather than sitting below it as a separate caption.

descriptions: Storm clouds, low buildings, a wall and a car establish the surrounding scene.
The tall concrete building narrows toward the upper edge.
A dark armed figure faces the tower from the foreground.
Large pale letterforms appear attached to the face of the building.
A short right-hand tagline and small festival and billing lines surround the scene.
the-raid.methodNote: The tower and foreground figure follow their visible silhouettes. Each slanted title letter is traced around its visible front face, retaining its concrete texture; the dark cast edges and adjacent masonry stay with the tower. Worn edges make this an analytical boundary, not a recovered text object. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Against a giant
connections.title: A small figure meets a huge vertical
connections.text: The dark foreground figure is much smaller than the tower. Looking up the narrowing building exaggerates that difference in scale.

connections.label: Letters as architecture
connections.title: The title inherits the building’s perspective
connections.text: The title is skewed to sit across the tower’s face. Its pale surfaces share the concrete texture, making the words feel embedded in the setting.

descriptions: The modern house and green lawn form a sharply organised domestic setting.
A dark-clothed standing figure occupies the right foreground.
Pale clothing and lounge furniture form a compact group farther back at the left.
A much smaller upright figure stands near the doorway.
Cropped bare legs and a small coloured ball interrupt the lawn.
The Korean title, small credits and upper notices surround the image.
parasite.methodNote: The people, reclining chair, cropped legs and coloured ball are traced from this exact Korean poster. Eye bars stay with the people. At this source resolution, thin chair tubing is isolated with its pale print while small lawn gaps remain in the background. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Three distances
connections.title: Different scales in one domestic scene
connections.text: The large standing figure, lounge group and smaller doorway figure establish three distances. Their different heights and poses break the house’s strict horizontal lines.

connections.label: Interruptions on the lawn
connections.title: Small details disturb the open green
connections.text: The bright ball is isolated in the grass, while cropped legs enter from the lower left without showing the rest of the body. Both interrupt the lawn’s otherwise open space.

descriptions: A strong yellow field surrounds both the review text and tree image.
The pink canopy and narrowing trunk create a single tree silhouette.
Dark eyes, hair, nose and mouth are blended into the tree form.
A blue panel gives the lower title its own colour field.
Pink script lettering and pale lower credits sit on the blue panel.
Centred review lines and a curved award line occupy the upper yellow space.
taste-of-cherry.methodNote: The tree and face are deliberately blended in the printed artwork. This study distinguishes the pink tree shape from locally visible dark facial features; the soft photographic transitions cannot be recovered as independent, complete face and tree originals. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two images in one
connections.title: A canopy also becomes a face
connections.text: The eyes occupy the canopy while the nose and mouth fall closer to the branching trunk. One outline therefore supports both a tree and a portrait reading.

connections.label: Pink across two fields
connections.title: The tree colour returns in the title
connections.text: Pink stands against yellow in the tree and against blue in the title. Repeating the colour connects the image above to the separate lettering panel below.

descriptions: The pale stage, fine perspective lines and photographed outer mount remain together.
A small head and black bodice sit high at the left.
Orange fabric, pale ruffles and black stockings expand the dancing silhouette.
The curved double bass sweeps from the right toward the lower left.
A large foreground hand and patterned sleeve overlap the instrument.
Pale and green display lettering sits within the illustrated frame.
jane-avril.methodNote: The dancer is divided at the bodice and billowing skirt, while the double bass and foreground hand are traced as overlapping printed silhouettes. The photographed mounting board stays with the background. Fine hatching and pale display letters share the paper tone, so their edges remain interpretive. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A repeated curve
connections.title: Skirt and instrument sweep in opposite directions
connections.text: The skirt pushes outward from the left while the bass curves down from the right and across the bottom. These two large curves hold the composition in motion.

connections.label: Near and far
connections.title: An oversized hand frames a small dancer
connections.text: The foreground hand is large beside the dancer’s head. The instrument and hand act as a close frame around the more distant performance.

descriptions: Warm plaster and floor tones give the sheet a continuous pale setting.
Two stacked lines of tall gold lettering fill the upper half.
A seated boy faces outward near the lower right.
A reclining woman rests across the boy’s lap and the foreground.
Small dark names and billing lines occupy the upper, left and lower margins.
central-station.methodNote: The visible boy and reclining woman are traced separately from the warm setting. Their bodies overlap, and the small installed reproduction has soft photographic edges; no obscured anatomy is reconstructed. The gold title is isolated within its actual letter area rather than lifting the entire upper panel. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two scales of intimacy
connections.title: A large title above a small shared space
connections.text: The gold title occupies almost the whole upper width, while the two people gather closely in the lower right. The difference in scale gives the quiet human scene room beneath the letters.

connections.label: Warm continuity
connections.title: Lettering and setting share a palette
connections.text: The ochre title repeats the warm tones of the wall and floor. The darker figures and small black credits provide contrast within that restrained palette.

descriptions: The warm printed field and the aged edge remain together.
The dark bridge, curved hull and tall rigging establish the upward viewpoint.
The white and blue flags interrupt the dark mast with sharp diagonals.
Small blue figures with raised arms gather on and around the ship.
The large Cyrillic announcements occupy the open sky above the bridge.
Light Cyrillic lettering and numerals curve across the dark lower hull.
battleship-potemkin.methodNote: Regional ink masks separate the flags, crowd and Cyrillic lettering from the ship-and-mast region. The upper-deck crowd follows the curved deck boundary, and orange background inside the mast region is excluded. Fine antialiased edges and rigging remain visible source pixels. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Upward energy
connections.title: Small figures, monumental ship
connections.text: The raised arms repeat the upward thrust of the mast while their scale makes the bridge appear immense.

connections.label: Bright interruptions
connections.title: Flags and lettering cut through the dark
connections.text: Pale flag shapes above and large pale letters below punctuate the blue-black mass of the ship.

descriptions: The photographed paper edges and pale mount stay at the rear.
A large yellow rectangle and its dark border give the small flock room to soar.
Black, grey and white facets form a diagonal flock near the top.
The newspaper name is the dominant dark wordmark near the foot.
The smaller lines above and below the name complete the message.
daily-herald-early-bird.methodNote: The mounted print is separated from its field, the complete regional bird motif and the two typographic levels. The flock retains every printed facet rather than separating it by colour. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Flight and space
connections.title: A small flock activates a large field
connections.text: The pointed birds concentrate movement near the top, while the uninterrupted yellow below lets that movement read clearly.

connections.label: Name and promise
connections.title: Two scales of type
connections.text: The newspaper name carries the visual weight; the smaller early-bird line connects the birds to the printed promise.

descriptions: The pale gold ground unifies the blended portrait montage.
The large face at the left looks out from behind the central figure.
The face and broad hat at the right balance the left portrait.
The headcloth, torso and light clothing make one tall central silhouette.
The widely spaced green LAGAAN wordmark anchors the montage.
Small production lines, the subtitle and the fine billing are retained together.
lagaan.methodNote: Traced visible silhouettes divide this blended photographic montage into three portrait groups. The pale clothing and softly dissolved shoulders retain a little adjacent gold where the printed image merges into its background. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Portrait hierarchy
connections.title: One full figure between two faces
connections.text: The central figure is shown further down the body, while the two enlarged faces create a broad, balanced backdrop.

connections.label: Warm image, cool name
connections.title: Green settles the golden montage
connections.text: The title is a strong cool accent beneath the warm skin tones and pale gold surroundings.

descriptions: The glowing sky fades into the dark lower ground around the title.
The small distant skyline and rough foreground grass share the left side.
The wall rises along the right edge behind the figure.
The crouching young man, his jacket and visible hands form the main silhouette.
The pale TSOTSI name and its smaller phonetic line sit in the dark foot.
tsotsi.methodNote: The figure and wall are traced separately; skyline and foreground grass remain a visible landscape group. The dark photographic fade is retained rather than reconstructed. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Near and far
connections.title: A crouching figure beside a distant city
connections.text: The figure occupies the right foreground; the smaller skyline opens a long view on the left.

connections.label: Light carried down
connections.title: Sunset gold returns in the title
connections.text: The bright sky and the pale title form two warm points around the darker figure.

descriptions: The outer field includes the blue edge and larger portrait repetitions beyond the nested panels.
The pink-red continental silhouette crosses the repeated rectangular structure.
Successive printed blue and pale panels retain the larger portrait echoes that are interwoven with them.
