Successive rectangular edges frame the portrait and create an inward rhythm.
The smallest red-and-cream portrait is the central point of recognition.
The multilingual heading and the lower-right mark remain together.
heroic-guerrilla.methodNote: This intentionally overprinted graphic retains the surrounding portraits inside their actual nested printed panels. The central portrait panel, visible pink continental motif, frame edges and commemorative text are separated. The large panel is a visible graphic structure, not a claimed isolated figure or reconstructed hidden layer. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Inward repetition
connections.title: Frames pull the eye toward a face
connections.text: The repeated rectangles become progressively smaller around the central red-and-cream portrait.

connections.label: Two overlapping motifs
connections.title: A map crosses a repeated portrait
connections.text: The continental silhouette travels across the rectangular image, linking a geographic shape to the face at the centre.

descriptions: A dark, red-lit star field remains behind the composition.
The large male portrait and orange suit dominate the upper-left image.
The green planetary curve sweeps across the lower half.
The small tethered astronaut and the visible spacecraft occupy the lower-right edge.
White actor, tagline, title and release lettering are kept together.
project-hail-mary.methodNote: The portrait, planetary curve and visible spacecraft/astronaut group are traced from this release artwork. Glowing edges and fine mixed-colour letter fringes retain their local printed light. Small green billing stays with the lower image surfaces; no hidden body, craft or background is reconstructed. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Scale shift
connections.title: A face and a tiny traveller
connections.text: The enormous portrait and the small suited astronaut create two different scales of human presence.

connections.label: A sweeping boundary
connections.title: The planet carries the eye into the title
connections.text: The green curve rises toward the spacecraft and brings the lower lettering into the same diagonal movement.

descriptions: The mottled green ground and small stars surround the portrait.
The rounded black bob makes a strong frame around the pale face.
The face and exposed neck form the brightest continuous shape.
The red cardigan and dark clothing create a broad base beneath the face.
The yellow handwritten film title crosses the lower portrait.
The actor names, director line and small billing are retained as lettering.
amelie.methodNote: The bob, exposed face and cardigan are separately traced, excluding green background wedges at their contours. Regional title and neutral-ink masks include the dim antialiased strokes of the director line and fine billing. The small installed source limits hair-edge precision; no new detail has been generated. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Framing the face
connections.title: Dark hair makes the pale face glow
connections.text: The simple dark curve around the face creates a concentrated point of contrast against the green ground.

connections.label: Warm accents
connections.title: Red clothing and yellow handwriting
connections.text: The cardigan and loose yellow title add two warm accents below the cooler green surroundings.

descriptions: The pale field dissolves around the portraits and deepens to ochre beneath the title.
The rear face and orange scarf occupy the upper-left of the portrait group.
The large bearded face, cap and wrapping scarf dominate the centre-right.
The small walking group crosses the fading lower edge of the portraits.
The compact, heavy YOL wordmark sits directly beneath the travellers.
The top announcement and the small lower billing remain together.
yol.methodNote: The two overlapping scarf-framed portraits and the small travelling group are divided by traced visible boundaries. Their softly faded surroundings remain with each group; the upper announcement is a distinct printed panel. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two human scales
connections.title: Faces above, travellers below
connections.text: The small walking group sits beneath the enlarged portraits, changing the scale without leaving the same fading image.

connections.label: A dense wordmark
connections.title: The title steadies the dissolving image
connections.text: The heavy black YOL lettering provides a firm base below the pale, fading portrait edges.

descriptions: Orange and blue fields and the printed frame remain behind the figures.
The left yellow figure covers its eyes, with a pink cross and surrounding movement marks.
The tall central figure covers its ears and carries a pink cross.
The right yellow figure covers its mouth, above another pink cross.
The dark top lettering reads IGNORANCE = FEAR.
The lower words, pink triangle and ACT UP message form a second line of force.
ignorance-equals-fear.methodNote: Regional ink masks retain each complete yellow figure, pink cross, black outline and its surrounding movement marks. Orange spaces remain in the field; the two textual bands are separated by their actual printed lettering. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Repeated gestures
connections.title: Three bodies make a visual sequence
connections.text: The figures repeat a shared yellow-and-pink treatment while changing the gesture from eyes to ears to mouth.

connections.label: Words frame the bodies
connections.title: The message is held above and below
connections.text: The top declaration and lower call to act bracket the three gestures, turning the figures into a linked argument.

descriptions: Flowing stripes, floral pattern and the decorative border make a continuous ground.
The seated woman bends toward the salad, her patterned sleeve curving across the lower image.
The standing woman holds a small morsel near her mouth; her long dress follows the right edge.
The large bowl and the salad at the foot make the product scene concrete.
Tall outlined DELFTSCHE SLAOLIE lettering spans the top.
The small geometric emblem occupies a quiet rectangle between the flowing patterns.
delftsche-slaolie.methodNote: Traced outlines separate the two women, salad bowl and central emblem from the densely interwoven ornament. Some hair and fabric decoration remains inseparable from the neighbouring printed pattern; the title plane contains its dark outlined letterforms. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Lines become gestures
connections.title: Hair, fabric and background share a rhythm
connections.text: The curved ornamental lines continue visually into the clothing and the bent posture of the seated woman.

connections.label: From name to use
connections.title: A product title above a domestic action
connections.text: The tall lettering names the product while the bowl and hands show a small scene of preparation and tasting.

descriptions: The white paper and pale photographic bedding create breathing room around the figures.
The man’s head, exposed torso and visible arms stay together, including the hand beside the woman’s hair.
The reclining woman’s head, raised arm and lower hand on the bedding form one visible figure.
The large red MAYNILA lettering climbs sharply from left to right.
The smaller subtitle and black billing repeat the title’s angle.
The restoration and festival information occupies the narrow top margin.
manila-in-the-claws-of-light.methodNote: The two visible figures are traced within the restored-edition photograph. Bedding and soft photographic edges remain with the pale ground; the diagonal title and supporting text are separated through their regional printed inks. Billing is confined to the observed diagonal text area and upper continuation rule, with photographic fragments returned to bedding. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A shared diagonal
connections.title: Bodies and title rise together
connections.text: The sloping portrait group and red title both move from the lower-left toward the upper-right.

connections.label: Quiet image, loud name
connections.title: One red interruption
connections.text: The large red wordmark breaks the restrained black-and-white photograph and pale surrounding paper.

descriptions: The cream ground separates the deliberately uneven blocks and fragments.
A warm, tightly cropped female face fills the upper-right panel.
The small running figure overlaps the space between the face and the title.
Blue, pink, yellow and grey blocks hold the large A, B, D and S initials.
The smaller black words complete the staggered French film title.
Actor names, the director line and the small lower credits remain together.
breathless.methodNote: The face panel is an explicit printed crop. The runner is isolated within a traced region using its blue-purple ink; the initial blocks retain their intended rectangular boundaries. Fine contours are limited by the small installed source. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Scales collide
connections.title: A huge face above a small runner
connections.text: The cropped face and the running figure bring two very different scales into the same tight composition.

connections.label: A title assembled in pieces
connections.title: Initials become coloured signs
connections.text: Oversized letters in coloured blocks join smaller black words, making the title move across several uneven lines.

descriptions: The golden station interior recedes toward a bright opening behind the characters.
The large suited man occupies the left foreground.
The smaller woman in a red jacket stands at the centre of the image.
The seated man at the right turns toward the central space.
White Spanish title lettering fills the dark lower centre.
The actor names, tagline, director line and small billing remain together.
secret-in-their-eyes.methodNote: Three visible character groups are traced within the blended station montage. The left jacket ends at its dark fade above the title; the separate warm photographic fragment below OJOS stays with the setting. Near-black fade pixels and overprinted campaign lettering are separated regionally. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Depth through scale
connections.title: Three figures establish three distances
connections.text: The large man at left, smaller central woman and turned seated man make the station feel deeper than a flat portrait row.

connections.label: A red centre
connections.title: One jacket catches the warm light
connections.text: The red jacket creates a concentrated accent within the gold interior and dark suits.

descriptions: The warm, lightly marked paper remains behind the portrait and letters.
The narrow red and blue rectangular border encloses the entire appeal.
The star-banded hat and directly facing head form the upper portrait.
The blue coat, pale shirt and red bow tie make a broad torso below.
The foreshortened pointing hand projects toward the viewer.
The large I WANT YOU and FOR U.S. ARMY lines use dark centres and red outlines.
The smaller nearest-recruiting-station line closes the message.
uncle-sam.methodNote: The hat-and-face silhouette, torso and pointing hand are traced separately. Regional ink masks isolate the enclosing border and two lettering levels; the printed paper is left intact as the complement. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Addressing the viewer
connections.title: The finger repeats the direct gaze
connections.text: The frontal eyes and foreshortened pointing hand both turn the appeal outward toward the person looking.

connections.label: A repeated palette
connections.title: Border and headline reinforce the figure
connections.text: Red and blue recur in the hat, clothes, frame and outlined recruiting words.

descriptions: The sandy field leaves a broad expanse around the tree and small person.
The wide canopy and visible branches stretch horizontally near the top.
A small dark standing figure gives the tree and open space a human scale.
Widely spaced green TIMBUKTU lettering anchors the lower field.
White review excerpts, small laurels and fine billing sit between and below the image and title.
The black-and-gold award banner is a distinct printed strip at the top.
timbuktu.methodNote: The canopy and branches are isolated within a traced tree region; the separate standing figure and regional lettering masks preserve the source’s unusually open composition. Fine leaves retain some sandy edge pixels. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Human scale
connections.title: A small figure beneath a wide canopy
connections.text: The tiny dark figure makes the tree appear expansive and the surrounding sandy field feel open.

connections.label: Horizontal calm
connections.title: Canopy and title share a wide span
connections.text: The wide tree above and the widely spaced title below repeat a quiet horizontal structure.

descriptions: The dark green field surrounds a pale, serrated circular frame.
The smiling lower-left face and patterned clothing rise from the bottom of the circle.
The smaller upper face tilts down into the group.
The larger right-hand portrait turns inward, with a raised hand near the face.
Small line drawings float in the pale spaces between the portraits.
The large flowing Bengali title spreads across the dark lower field.
Smaller Bengali production lines appear above and below the main image and title.
pather-panchali.methodNote: Three visible portrait silhouettes and the small line-drawn motifs are separated inside the printed circular frame. The title is isolated from the dark green field. The installed edition’s limited resolution makes the finest outlines approximate. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: An inward circle
connections.title: Three faces gather inside one frame
connections.text: The portraits turn and tilt toward the middle, while the circular frame holds them as a close group.

connections.label: Two kinds of line
connections.title: Small drawings and large lettering
connections.text: Fine drawn motifs occupy the pale circle; broad flowing Bengali letterforms spread across the dark lower field.

descriptions: A pale blue and red split field surrounds the portrait inside a cream border.
The complete face and neck retain all of their internal red, cream and blue modelling.
The dark suit, pale shirt and red tie form the broad lower silhouette.
The small circular badge sits on the right lapel.
The large pale blue HOPE letters cross the dark block at the foot.
obama-hope.methodNote: The portrait and clothing are traced as semantic shapes, keeping the full red-blue-cream modelling inside each. The badge and actual HOPE letterforms are isolated regionally; no colour is treated as a standalone portrait layer. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Gaze and promise
connections.title: The upward face leads to one word
connections.text: The upward-angled gaze and the large, plain HOPE wordmark concentrate the image around a person and a short message.

connections.label: Small emblem, broad palette
connections.title: The lapel badge repeats the surrounding colours
connections.text: The small circular badge echoes red, pale blue and cream already used across the portrait and background.

descriptions: The red printed field and the wear in this particular scan remain together.
The small white crown sits alone above the instruction.
The first two lines form one emphatic instruction.
The much smaller connecting word makes a pause in the message.
The last two lines repeat the weight and spacing of the first instruction.
keep-calm.methodNote: White ink is isolated from the red scan within the crown and the three meaningful word groups; the original printed texture is retained. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Authority and address
connections.title: A small emblem, a large command
connections.text: The compact crown shares the same central axis as the much larger words, giving the instruction a steady vertical structure.

connections.label: A measured pause
connections.title: The smallest word controls the rhythm
connections.text: The short AND sits between two broad pairs of lines. Its smaller size makes a visual pause without breaking the centred alignment.

descriptions: Paper, folds and the black title-panel ground hold the printed layout together.
The overhead street scene includes small figures and the foreground debris on its left.
A cropped face occupies the upper right at a much larger scale than the people in the street.
The yellow-tinted lower montage remains a visible printed group of overlapping images.
The red title letters are separated along their visible ink, including their broken edges.
The white wire and the small lettering within the black panel form a finer register.
battle-of-algiers.methodNote: The photograph already uses discrete montage panels. Those visible photographic groups stay intact; only the red lettering and the fine wire/panel text are isolated by their ink. Folds and photographic panel edges are not repaired. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Near and far
connections.title: A face beside a street
connections.text: The enormous face and the much smaller street figures occupy adjacent panels, making two different scales of looking immediately visible.

connections.label: Letters and wire
connections.title: Two kinds of sharp edge
connections.text: The broken red letters sit above a thin white wire. Their jagged edges make a visual connection even though their thickness and colour differ.

descriptions: The broad white field sets the compact imagery apart from the page edges.
The several blue-tinted photographs remain together as the printed image strip.
The heavy yellow word is the brightest large shape on the sheet.
The finer, darker express lettering overlaps the heavier title.
The reviews, tagline and billing form small, widely spaced groups around the central image.
chungking-express.methodNote: The blue montage follows its printed, irregular border; it is not separated into invented scenes. Regional colour isolation distinguishes the two overlapping title treatments and the small text from the white paper. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Weight and lightness
connections.title: Two voices in one title
connections.text: The bulky yellow word and the finer dark express lettering overlap. Their difference in weight is as noticeable as their difference in colour.

connections.label: Colour in a narrow space
connections.title: A bright title above a cool strip
connections.text: The yellow title and the compressed blue montage make a concentrated centre, while the white field leaves room for both to register.

descriptions: The ochre room, chair and small lower imprints remain the supporting field.
The performer at upper left is shown without her head, as in the original composition.
The thinly drawn instruments and musicians remain a connected orchestral group.
The man, his hat, beard and cane make a narrow group behind the woman.
The feathered hat, face, hands and sweeping black dress belong to the foreground spectator.
The dark outline of the venue name and the address make a lighter verbal presence above the figures.
divan-japonais.methodNote: Hand-traced contours separate the visible spectators, the cropped stage performer and the orchestra. The chair and room stay behind them. The seated woman is one connected visual subject even though her visible hand and hat are separated by other printed marks. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Audience and stage
connections.title: The spectator outweighs the performer
connections.text: The broad dark dress and feathered hat occupy much more of the sheet than the cropped performer at upper left, reversing the usual balance between audience and stage.

connections.label: Mass and line
connections.title: A solid silhouette beside an outlined orchestra
connections.text: The woman’s dark body is visually heavy. The orchestra beside it is described with much thinner marks, allowing the foreground figure to dominate.

descriptions: The teal atmosphere is the continuous ground behind the assembled portraits.
The largest head and its visible dark collar occupy the top of the portrait arrangement.
The portraits on the left step down in scale and overlap one another.
The right portraits and the raised hand make another descending cluster.
The hooded figure occupies the front of the ensemble and fades into the mist below; the small overprinted tagline stays with this group.
The desert floor, horizon, small walking figure and fine billing make a separate change of scale.
The geometric DUNE title, upper actor names and release line are separated where visible.
dune.methodNote: This low-resolution photographic montage has soft, merged edges. Contours group visible portraits on each side rather than claiming independent cutouts of every person; the hooded foreground and walking figure retain only their visible artwork. Some mist stays attached at the dissolving boundaries. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Scale changes
connections.title: Portraits above a tiny walker
connections.text: The largest face and the small figure near the desert horizon make a dramatic scale contrast within one vertically stacked composition.

connections.label: Complexity and simplicity
connections.title: A crowded ensemble above spare letters
connections.text: The overlapping portrait groups are visually dense; the widely spaced geometric title gives the eye a quieter rhythm below them.

descriptions: The aged paper and dark outer border remain intact.
The masthead includes the red printed panel and its cream letterforms.
The cap, face and moustache form a portrait directed toward the viewer.
The foreshortened hand and the dark sleeve project toward the lower left.
The smaller appeal leads to the much larger outlined YOU.
The red magazine name and price repeat below the portrait, with the printer line.
kitchener.methodNote: The cap, head and pointing sleeve follow their illustrated contours. Lettering is isolated by its printed ink; the masthead stays with its actual red panel. Paper between the outlined YOU letters remains in the background. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two direct addresses
connections.title: The finger and the word YOU
connections.text: The pointing hand projects toward the viewer while the largest word makes the same direct address in type.

connections.label: A frame of red
connections.title: The publication appears twice
connections.text: The large masthead and the smaller red price line frame the central portrait, making the magazine advertisement visible as part of the design.

descriptions: The blue painted atmosphere, dark supporting shapes and paper border remain behind the subjects.
The large blue face and visible collar establish the dominant portrait scale.
A smaller pale profile appears behind the large blue face.
The blonde figure is shown at full length in a black dress.
The red and pale fabric sweeps away from the woman through the lower centre.
The yellow title and upper director lettering create two bright stops.
The blue billing and smaller bottom imprints supply a denser lower edge.
la-dolce-vita.methodNote: The visible painted figures and fabric are traced as illustrated shapes. The two male profiles remain distinct, while only visible portions of the woman and fabric are assigned; dark blends at the painted edges are analytical boundaries. Yellow title ink and blue billing are isolated regionally. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Unequal portrait scales
connections.title: A full figure beside a cropped face
connections.text: The woman’s full-length figure is set beside a much larger face. The mismatch in scale makes the printed encounter feel deliberately assembled.

connections.label: A moving accent
connections.title: Red fabric between cool portrait and yellow type
connections.text: The curved red fabric moves through the lower centre, linking the standing figure to the bold yellow title across the blue ground.

descriptions: The nearly black field leaves a large unresolved interval between the portraits.
The large face is cut by the left edge of the sheet.
The smaller man, visible shirt and hand occupy the opposite edge.
The white Korean title spans the central darkness.
The subdued taglines and release information remain a finer, quieter register.
oldboy.methodNote: Hand-traced visible contours separate the two photographed figures from the black field. Their black clothing and hair merge into that field, so those boundaries are a reading of the visible montage rather than recovered studio cutouts. Free-standing title and copy are isolated; the first small tagline characters that cross the face remain with that portrait. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: An unequal encounter
connections.title: Two faces at opposite scales
connections.text: The cropped foreground face and the smaller face at the opposite edge never settle into a shared photographic room; scale and position create their relationship.

connections.label: A bridge of type
connections.title: White letters span the dark interval
connections.text: The title crosses the open black area between the figures. Its brightness makes that empty interval an active part of the composition.

descriptions: The light paper, thin frame and printing texture remain the supporting sheet.
A large black diagonal turns the sheet into an asymmetric field.
The pale circle is a distinct geometric shape within the black field.
The large red triangle drives into the circle from the upper left.
The small bars, wedges, pale strokes and grey blocks repeat the larger geometric action.
The words change angle, size and position around the main shapes.
red-wedge.methodNote: The principal triangle, circle and diagonal field are traced from this reproduction. Regional ink tests separate the words and smaller geometric interventions. The texture of the pale circle is preserved rather than replaced with a digitally perfect fill. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A collision of shapes
connections.title: The triangle enters the circle
connections.text: The long point of the red wedge crosses into the pale circle. The contact turns static geometry into an immediately readable direction of movement.

connections.label: Repetition and direction
connections.title: Small marks echo the large wedge
connections.text: The smaller red bars and wedges repeat the main triangle’s pointed, directional character, spreading the movement through the page.

descriptions: The warm, softly lit ground remains behind the two portraits.
The softer male portrait occupies the upper right behind the foreground figure; the overprinted award copy stays attached.
The sharply focused face, headscarf and visible shoulder form one foreground subject, retaining the fine billing over them.
The pale title crosses the lower part of the photographic composition.
Three small review groups occupy the open area above the portraits.
a-separation.methodNote: The two photographic portraits follow their visible silhouettes, with the foreground scarf determining the shared edge. Title letter contours are traced at the native low resolution to preserve their translucency without extracting the pale shoulder behind them. Reviews separate above; the tiny award copy and billing remain attached to the portraits they cross. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Near but separate
connections.title: Focus makes two depths
connections.text: The woman’s sharp features sit directly in front of a softer male portrait. The difference in focus creates depth even where their silhouettes almost touch.

connections.label: Faces and quiet type
connections.title: Expression carries the centre
connections.text: The title spans the lower image while the two faces occupy the main field above it. Its muted pale tone keeps the expressions visually prominent.

descriptions: The green printed ground and small black overprinted words keep the extremely narrow sheet intact.
The pale buildings provide a small architectural counterpoint to the huge figure.
The dark torso and tapering lower silhouette fill most of the vertical format.
Pale eyes and teeth puncture the small, dark head.
The extended clawed hands cross the body in long, thin shapes.
The pale title and its curved rules climb around the figure.
The pale lower credits and round emblem form the foot of the sheet.
nosferatu.methodNote: The narrow, coarse reproduction is divided into visible drawn forms: curved title, head, torso, claws, town and lower credits. Pale ink is isolated only within the relevant title, town and credit regions; tiny printed texture stays in its original position. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A title follows a body
connections.title: The name bends around the silhouette
connections.text: The title rises along the left side and curves above the head. Its path reinforces the pressure of the figure inside the narrow sheet.

connections.label: A few bright marks
connections.title: Eyes above tiny windows
connections.text: The pale eyes and teeth are small but striking against the dark head. The lighter town provides a second, smaller-scale group of marks below them.

descriptions: The painted space, sweeping ground and white paper border provide the continuous setting.
The huge mask occupies the background at a scale far larger than the foreground figures.
The Death Star and the descending fleet remain a visible painted group.
The two central figures and their painted fabric make a bright triangular arrangement.
The two small droids broaden the base of the foreground group.
The white blade, burst and horizontal flare form the main luminous axis.
The title, upper tagline and lower billing are the printed verbal layer.
star-wars.methodNote: The painted montage is grouped along visible contours, retaining the original glow and brushwork. Luke and Leia remain a connected illustrated group, and the fleet retains some surrounding painted atmosphere. The flare is isolated as printed light; unseen bodies and mask areas are not reconstructed. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A luminous axis
connections.title: The raised blade links two scales
connections.text: The lightsaber rises from the small foreground figure into the enormous mask behind it. The bright cross-shaped flare makes that vertical link unmistakable.

connections.label: A broadening base
connections.title: Companions make a triangle
connections.text: The raised figure narrows the group at the top; Leia and the small droids widen it below, making the crowded foreground readable as a triangle.

descriptions: The monochrome paper, border and small printer marks remain together; there is no advertising headline in this impression.
The long, dark cloak creates the largest connected shape on the sheet.
The scarf crosses the shoulder and drops as a pale, tapering form over the cloak.
The small profile and hair are framed between hat and scarf.
The broad dark hat extends well beyond the face.
The gloved hand and diagonal cane appear at the lower left of the figure.
aristide-bruant.methodNote: Contours follow the hat, complete visible profile and gray hair beneath the brim, scarf, cloak and lower glove in this monochrome museum reproduction. The study describes shape and overlap, not the original print’s colours. Printer marks are kept on the paper plane rather than treated as an absent advertising title. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: A small face, broad forms
connections.title: The profile sits between hat and scarf
connections.text: The comparatively small face gains emphasis from two much larger shapes: the wide hat above it and the scarf crossing beneath it.

connections.label: A turn through the silhouette
connections.title: The scarf interrupts the cloak
connections.text: The pale scarf bends over the shoulder and drops across the dark cloak, leading the eye back from the large body toward the turned head.

descriptions: The monochrome sheet, outer border and small lower printer mark form the ground.
The publication name, address and subscription information occupy the right side.
The tall feathered hat and its pale brim make an elaborate upper silhouette.
The small face and soft fur collar interrupt the darker hat and dress.
The broad dotted dress, sleeve and visible lower hand create the main body shape.
The furry muff held out at the right makes a separate projecting form.
la-revue-blanche.methodNote: This is a monochrome museum reproduction. Hand-traced shapes distinguish hat, face and collar, dress and muff; regional dark-ink isolation separates the lettering. Fur and feather edges remain approximate readings of the fine printed marks, without adding missing fibres or claiming the original palette. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two masses share a page
connections.title: Lettering balances the dress
connections.text: The publication name and the broad dotted dress occupy different sides of the sheet. Their separated dark masses make the figure and the publication readable together.

connections.label: Light interrupts dark
connections.title: Face and collar sit between hat and dress
connections.text: The pale face and fur collar separate two dark shapes, creating a small bright centre below the elaborate hat.

descriptions: The warm-coloured sheet remains visible around the illustration and through the spaces between printed marks.
The cat is one visible group, including the pale eyes, fine whiskers, rough fur edge, claws and continuous curled tail.
Fine red curves and circular lettering form the medallion behind the cat; the occluded part is not reconstructed.
The upper announcement, large company name and small Paris printer line retain their black printed strokes.
The smaller red wording identifies the company and describes the advertised programme beside the silhouette.
The lower red panel and its irregular printed border remain behind the tail and separate name lettering.
The mixed-scale Rodolphe Salis name and small AVEC are separated from the red panel, retaining the visible overlap with the tail.
le-chat-noir.methodNote: Traced source contours keep the visible cat, whiskers, eyes, claws and curled tail together. The red medallion and printed words are isolated within their observed locations, and the lower panel is an actual printed shape. Fine ink edges retain the limits of this 516 × 800 reproduction. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Name and image
connections.title: One black cat, two kinds of identity
connections.text: The large dark silhouette and the large words CHAT NOIR occupy opposite sides. Their shared ink weight makes the pictured animal and the company name easy to compare.

connections.label: Two kinds of curve
connections.title: A fine circle above a heavy curl
connections.text: The red medallion wraps around the head with many fine lines, while the tail curves broadly across the lower panel. Their related directions work at very different weights.

connections.label: A named programme
connections.title: From company to a named participant
connections.text: The smaller red programme wording leads toward a separate red panel with Rodolphe Salis’s name. Changes of colour and scale divide the information into stages.

labels: Totoro: ears, whiskers, body and feet
descriptions: The dark forest, visible rain, reflected ground and unprinted margins surround the waiting figures.
The circular sign, visible timetable and post, and concrete base form the bus-stop assembly.
The girl, red canopy, visible umbrella handles, clothing and both boots remain together.
The complete visible grey figure includes pointed ears, fine whiskers, paws and feet.
The small green leaf and its upward stem sit on the much larger head.
The bright pink title occupies the upper-right forest.
The actual white top panel, vertical white slogan and legible footer credit pixels carry the campaign wording.
my-neighbor-totoro.methodNote: Visible contours retain each waiting figure, the leaf and the bus-stop assembly. Rain remains on the surface where it is printed; overprinted words leave text-shaped gaps. Fine JPEG edge fringes remain visible. The girl is deliberately not identified as a named film character. These are analytical divisions of the visible artwork, not original production layers. No artwork hidden behind another element is invented.

connections.label: Two shelters
connections.title: A broad umbrella and a small leaf
connections.text: Compare the red canopy above the small figure with the leaf above the larger one. Their different sizes make a shared response to rain visible.

connections.label: At the same stop
connections.title: A sign joins unequal figures
connections.text: The weathered sign and concrete base locate the meeting. Both figures stand on the wet ground beside this ordinary piece of street furniture.

descriptions: The blue-green atmosphere narrows beside the hull and meets the graduated advertising ground below. The photographed sheet edge stays with this supporting plane; the empty ship-shaped area is left transparent rather than filled in.

The prow, cream upper decks, funnel, mast and red waterline remain together as one towering object. Its near symmetry and steep edges make the viewer’s position feel low, while the painted light changes across the bow.

The small pale bird marks cluster against the dark left side of the hull. Their minute size makes the liner feel immense; they are retained at the source’s native resolution, so separation cannot disclose new feather detail.

The tall cream NORMANDIE letters form a second monumental shape below the prow. Their straight vertical rhythm steadies the pointed ship above while the open counters still reveal the darker printed ground.

The compact dark company line and the cream French Line script use different kinds of lettering within the same narrow area. Keeping these marks together lets their contrast be compared with the much larger ship name.

The reddish route and service lines spread below the operator’s names. Their smaller, spaced capitals change the reading from a single memorable name to a sequence of destinations and practical promises.
normandie.methodNote: Six analytical separations follow the visible liner, individually bounded bird marks and three distinct typographic roles. The bottom text is selected by ink colour within its own zones; it is not detached as opaque horizontal strips. Every original pixel appears once. No sky, sea, paper or hull hidden by another element has been reconstructed.
limitations: The liner contour is hand traced and may carry a very thin painted edge or neighbouring background pixel.
The birds contain only a few dozen visible pixels each; dark antialiasing at their edges may stay with the hull.
The operator line and script overlap visually and are kept together; neither is reconstructed beneath the other.
The source is a photographed sheet with wear and borders; those are preserved.

descriptions: The atmospheric ground holds the dark sky, coloured smoke and fire around the larger forms.
The hand-traced region keeps Godzilla’s visible head, textured body and limbs together, with overprinted lettering assigned separately.
The enormous red Japanese title and its pale outlines form a second giant shape along the left edge.
The orange beam and three visible aircraft give the confrontation a diagonal direction through the poster.
Buildings, portraits and the lower scene remain grouped as a montage, rather than being presented as isolated objects.
The top line, vertical slogans, cast and production credits, lower imprint and round emblem form the printed information plane.
godzilla.methodNote: Six analytical groups follow the visible monster, title, beam and aircraft, surrounding atmosphere, human/city montage and printed information. Where dark shapes and smoke merge, the hand-traced boundary is approximate. Lettering is separated from the illustration where the source supports it.
limitations: The lower monster contour merges into dark montage imagery; this is a manually bounded visible region, not a recovered original cutout.
Caption pixels include a one-pixel fringe from the actual source so anti-aliased outlines travel with the lettering; a few small printed or illustrated edge pixels remain ambiguous.
The city, portraits and lower scene intentionally remain a scene grouping, not individually extracted figures.
The beam/aircraft plane is about two percent of the sheet but carries a distinct visible action and three separate aircraft; no plane was added merely to increase the count.

descriptions: The cream intervals make the black lines legible and remain visible inside letters and rings. The outer photographed edge stays with this support plane; the cream shapes are actual source pixels, not a newly painted background.

Parallel black contours spread across the square and bend around the central lettering. Their spacing makes the surrounding field seem to vibrate, so the identity influences much more than the middle of the sheet.

The selected central contours make the MEXICO 68 reading easier to inspect beside the surrounding line field. This is a deliberately bounded reading region: the long M, X and I strokes continue beyond it in the original, and no independent original wordmark layer is claimed.

Blue, black, red, yellow and green ring strokes cross the numerals and interrupt the optical pattern. The black ring is selected by its circular position as well as brightness, so it remains with the coloured rings instead of disappearing into the surrounding black line field.
mexico-1968.methodNote: Four analytical views distinguish the paper, the outer optical field, a traced central reading region and the visible five-ring emblem. The lettering and its radiating lines are physically continuous in this image, so their division is a chosen interpretive boundary rather than a recovered object or print plate. Pixels hidden at crossings are never invented, and every visible source pixel appears exactly once.
limitations: The wordmark and field are one continuous graphic system; separating them requires a disclosed reading boundary, especially across the extended M, X and I strokes.
Black ring strokes intersect black numeral contours, so individual source pixels at their crossings cannot establish which shape was printed above the other.
JPEG antialiasing and colour bleed can leave faint edge pixels in an adjacent plane.
Paper and ink division follows a luminance threshold within the spatially defined composition; it is not a physical separation of printing plates.

descriptions: A large pale field and lavender, watercolour-like washes occupy most of the sheet. Separating this open space from the lettering makes its generous scale and irregular, cloudlike edges easier to notice.

Distant towers and tightly packed buildings establish a city beyond the balcony. Their soft detail contrasts with the nearer faces and pointing hand; the visible skyline is retained without fabricating buildings hidden by the figures.
The weathered concrete rail runs diagonally from the lower edge toward the pair. Its close texture and strong direction bridge the distant city and the small human scene.

The boy, his complete pointing hand and arm, and his companion stay together as one visible group. Their overlap matters: the gesture reaches across the woman toward the city, so keeping the pair intact preserves the relationship that gives the image its direction.

The uneven black ILO ILO letters float in the broad pale field, with the smaller director credit beneath them. Their brush-like edges introduce an informal rhythm above the orderly horizontal lines of the city.

Festival laurels and review quotations form a second, much smaller level of typography around the title. This plane makes the campaign’s dense evidence of acclaim visible separately from the intimate photograph below.
ilo-ilo.methodNote: Analytical partitions of the flattened source poster, not recovered production layers: every decoded source pixel belongs to exactly one native-resolution PNG, and obscured artwork is not reconstructed. Fine white credits printed over the photograph stay with their photographic regions, so the lettering separates with those regions in the opened view.
limitations: The 500 × 741 source limits fine detail; no upscaling or new detail is included in the delivered planes.
The defocused skyline has no perfectly sharp boundary; its hand-traced split follows the visible transition through the source blur.
The boy and companion share a plane to preserve their overlapping silhouettes and the complete pointing gesture.

Fine white credits printed over the photograph remain with their underlying photographic regions and therefore separate into fragments when those regions move; no clean background or hidden letters have been invented.
Bounded text extraction retains a one-source-pixel antialiased edge adjoining the type cores, which can include a small amount of the pale source background.

descriptions: A pale sky, a long palace facade and a crowd make a comparatively quiet setting behind the dancers. Keeping these visible background pixels together shows how the two bodies stand apart from a distant, mostly horizontal scene.

The floorboards and cast shadows make a firm base beneath the bent knees and lifted boots. The shadows stay on the stage rather than following the dancers forward, revealing a useful distinction between a figure and its trace on a surface.

The left dancer remains a complete visible silhouette, from the small raised finger to the boot kicked behind the other leg. The crossing sleeves, bent knee and folds give this one body a zigzag rhythm that can be followed independently.

The right dancer repeats the lifted heel and crossed-arm gesture with a different lean and spacing. Comparing the two intact figures makes the poster’s paired rhythm visible without pretending their poses are identical.

The heavy metallic RRR mark tilts above the figures, balancing their slender limbs with a broad, solid mass. Its open letter counters remain transparent to the visible sky pixels on the background plane.
rrr.methodNote: Analytical partitions of the flattened source poster, not recovered production layers: every decoded source pixel belongs to exactly one native-resolution PNG, and obscured artwork is not reconstructed.
limitations: The 500 × 740 source limits fine detail; no upscaling or new detail is included in the delivered planes.
A narrow fringe can remain where JPEG pixels blend a figure or letter edge with the background; those mixed pixels retain their original colours.
Small top campaign marks stay with the setting, and tiny bottom distributor marks stay with the stage; these are not claimed as a separate printing plate.

readings.label: Compare the scale
readings.title: A small flock. An immense ship.
readings.text: The pale birds sit against the dark hull. Follow the connection between these tiny marks and the towering prow, then fold the poster together to see how that contrast establishes scale.

readings.label: Ship → name → route
readings.title: From an image to a journey
readings.text: The pointed liner leads down into a broad, steady name. Below it, smaller lettering changes the reading from a memorable ship to a service and its destinations.

readings.label: Two giant forms
readings.title: A monster and a title share the stage
readings.text: The tall red lettering rises beside Godzilla’s textured body. Opening the planes lets you compare their scale and direction; folding them shows how closely the two shapes compete for attention.

readings.label: Trace the confrontation
readings.title: A diagonal cuts through the scene
readings.text: The beam and aircraft cross the atmosphere around the monster. The lower city and human montage bring that large confrontation back to a smaller, inhabited scale.

readings.label: Words become a field
readings.title: The lettering continues into its surroundings
readings.text: The central MEXICO68 reading and the surrounding parallel contours are visually continuous. Their separation is an analytical choice: bringing them together reveals how the wordmark shapes the whole field.

readings.label: Find the colour
readings.title: Five rings interrupt the optical rhythm
readings.text: The ring strokes cross the numerals within a mostly black-and-cream field. Their compact colour accents create a different point of attention inside the much larger pattern.

readings.label: Follow the gesture
readings.title: A small gesture opens onto a city
readings.text: The boy’s pointing arm stays with his companion as one human group. Trace it outward towards the distant buildings, then follow the balcony rail back to the pair.

readings.label: Space around the title
readings.title: A quiet photograph beneath a generous sky
readings.text: The irregular title occupies a broad pale field above the small human scene. The festival marks and review quotations supply another, finer scale of lettering around it.

readings.label: Follow the paired rhythm
readings.title: Two bodies, one visual beat
readings.text: The two dancers repeat bent knees, crossing arms and lifted heels without making identical silhouettes. Trace their separate poses, then bring the planes together to see the rhythm they create as a pair.

readings.label: Bodies and their shadows
readings.title: The dancers move; the stage holds them
readings.text: The figures come forward while their cast shadows remain on the floor. The broad metallic title sits above both dancers, balancing the lighter shapes of their moving limbs.
